title: Napoleonic Batavia Republic
capsule: The Batavian Republic's administration of the Cape Colony (1803–1806) began when Britain returned the territory under the Peace of Amiens (signed 1802, handover 1 March 1803). The Batavian government — by then a French satellite — nationalised the former VOC and placed the Cape under direct state rule from The Hague, appointing Jacob Abraham de Mist as commissioner-general (1803–1804) and Jan Willem Janssens as governor (1804–1806). De Mist introduced Enlightenment-influenced reforms including freedom of religion and a restructured judicial system. The interlude ended when a British expeditionary force defeated Janssens at the Battle of Blaauwberg on 8 January 1806, permanently returning the Cape to British control formalised by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The geographic extent of the Batavian Cape Colony is well documented through colonial administrative records; its interior frontiers with Xhosa territories were contested and not precisely fixed.
